nodes.label: Testing Guidelines
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: Name the scenario, assert one behavior, show the public API in doc tests, and snapshot generated output with cargo insta.

nodes.label: Apollo Rust Best Practices Handbook
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: The skill applies Apollo GraphQL's Rust Best Practices Handbook when writing, reviewing, or tuning Rust.

nodes.label: Generics and Dispatch
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: Keep static dispatch on hot paths. Use dyn Trait only for heterogeneous collections, and box at the API boundary rather than inside.

nodes.label: Type State Pattern
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: Phantom type parameters make illegal operations unrepresentable, so only Connection<Connected> can send.

nodes.label: Borrowing and Ownership
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: Prefer &T, &str, and &[T] over clone unless ownership must move. Small Copy values up to 24 bytes may pass by value. Use Cow when ownership is ambiguous.

nodes.label: Performance Guidelines
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: Benchmark release builds, run clippy perf lints, avoid clones in loops, and prefer iterators over intermediate collect calls.

nodes.label: Clippy Linting Workflow
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: Deny warnings for all targets and features with a locked Cargo.lock. Prefer expect over allow, with a justification, for redundant_clone, large_enum_variant, and needless_collect.

nodes.label: Error Handling Guidelines
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: Return Result for fallible work. Do not unwrap or expect outside tests. Libraries use thiserror, binaries may use anyhow, and ? replaces match chains.

nodes.label: Documentation Guidelines
nodes.author: apollographql
nodes.rationale: Line comments explain why. Doc comments explain what and how. Every TODO cites an issue. Libraries deny missing_docs.

nodes.label: DomainError
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: thiserror enum in core/src/domain/errors.rs. code() returns SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE so presentation maps stable codes to exits without parsing prose.

nodes.label: Exit Codes
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: 0 is success, 1 is a business or runtime DomainError, and 2 is usage or clap validation. Mapping stays in presentation so core never exits the process.

nodes.label: Split-Core Hexagonal CLI Architecture
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: Business logic lives in the core crate; the cli crate implements port traits and thin clap handlers. One process has one di.rs and one command tree. One action is one use case whose execute parameter is always named port. Formatters own stdout, DomainError codes map to exits in presentation, and use cases are tested in core so the binary stays a thin edge.

nodes.label: AppContext
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: Sole composition root in cli/src/di.rs. Manual Arc<dyn Port> wiring replaces a global service locator so every adapter is explicit and replaceable in tests.

nodes.label: clap
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: Derive macros live only in presentation commands. Core must not see clap types, so the domain stays free of the argument parser.

nodes.label: cli crate
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: The deployable unit: adapters, clap handlers, formatters, and the composition root. Terminal I/O stays in presentation so use cases remain free of stdio.

nodes.label: core crate
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: Contracts live in domain/ and use case structs live in usecases/. Core never depends on cli so codegen, tests, and later binaries can reuse the domain without the CLI.

nodes.label: Formatter
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: Formatters write stdout. Use cases must not print, so JSON and human output stay pipe-friendly and unit-testable.

nodes.label: Dependencies Point Inward
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: cli depends on core and core never depends on cli, so business rules stay reusable by other workspace members without pulling in clap or process exit.

nodes.label: Port Traits
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: Traits are owned by the domain. clap, stdio, and databases stay in cli. Use cases depend on Arc<dyn Port> so business code never names a concrete adapter.

nodes.label: Use Case
nodes.author: tous-secouristes-services
nodes.rationale: One action is one struct with a single execute method. The parameter is always named port so handlers, tests, and DI share one shape. A subcommand maps to one use case.

nodes.label: assert and assert_eq
nodes.rationale: Failure text should show actual versus expected. matches! with assert! checks a variant without full equality. Prefer a Result check over should_panic.

nodes.label: cargo nextest
nodes.rationale: nextest does not execute doc tests, so cargo test --doc still has to run.

nodes.label: pretty_assertions
nodes.rationale: pretty_assertions replaces assert_eq and assert_ne with colored diffs.

nodes.label: rstest
nodes.rationale: rstest cuts case boilerplate, but a single case is harder for people and IDEs to run, and the case name visually leads the condition.

nodes.label: testcontainers
nodes.rationale: testcontainers supplies external state for integration tests that need real services.

nodes.label: Criterion
nodes.rationale: Criterion benchmarks live in benches/ with harness = false. black_box stops the compiler from deleting the work.

nodes.label: mockall
nodes.rationale: automock builds a trait mock so a unit test can isolate a collaborator. Do not mock when an integration test is feasible.

nodes.label: proptest
nodes.rationale: Property tests assert invariants over generated inputs, such as encode/decode round trips and sort preserving length and order, with custom strategies for domain values.

nodes.label: Comments for Context
nodes.rationale: Comments should say why: safety, performance, or an external constraint. Names, small functions, tests, ADRs, and doc comments should carry what and how, because inline comments rot.

nodes.label: Test Error Paths
nodes.rationale: Many errors lack PartialEq, so tests compare Display text, or the value itself when Eq is implemented.

nodes.label: Doc Tests
nodes.rationale: Rustdoc examples run under cargo test but not cargo nextest, so nextest users still run cargo test --doc. Overlap with private tests is acceptable. Happy paths belong here.

nodes.label: Integration Tests
nodes.rationale: Files under tests/ see only the public API and check that units work together, including side effects. Split binary crates so logic lives in the library.

nodes.label: One Assertion per Test
nodes.rationale: Several assertions hide which behavior failed. Split behaviors, or share one assertion across rstest cases.

nodes.label: Snapshot Testing
nodes.rationale: insta compares output to a committed golden file. That fits generated or structural output, not stable scalars, critical logic, or flaky external data. Redact unstable fields and review the diff.

nodes.label: Tests as Living Documentation
nodes.rationale: A clear test often explains intended use better than the function body. Names should state the unit, the expected behavior, and the state under test.

nodes.label: Unit Tests
nodes.rationale: A #[cfg(test)] module beside the code can see private items and should cover one state, including errors and edges. ignore marks unfinished tests. should_panic is only for a panic contract.

nodes.label: Async Tests
nodes.rationale: tokio::test runs async tests. Do not sleep. Use channels, barriers, or tokio::time::pause, and tokio::time::timeout for deadlines.

nodes.label: CI Test Pipeline
nodes.rationale: CI should run fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test, and llvm-cov with a fail-under-lines gate.

nodes.label: Test Coverage
nodes.rationale: cargo-llvm-cov reports line coverage. Targets are 100 percent for critical logic, 90 percent or more for the public API, and 80 percent or more in general. Exclude generated code and FFI bindings.

nodes.label: Doc Tests
nodes.rationale: Examples under /// run as tests and show intended use. no_run compiles samples that have side effects. An Errors section documents the Err cases.

nodes.label: Integration Tests
nodes.rationale: Each file under tests/ is its own binary and uses only the public API. Prefer that over mocking every collaborator.

nodes.label: Panic and Result Testing
nodes.rationale: Prefer Result::is_err and matches! over should_panic. should_panic is for a real panic, optionally with an expected message. Tests may return Result and use ?.

nodes.label: RED-GREEN-REFACTOR
nodes.rationale: Write a failing test first, often against todo!, then the smallest code that passes, then refactor while the suite stays green.

nodes.label: Tests as Documentation
nodes.rationale: Tests show how the code is meant to be used, so they have to stay clear and current.

nodes.label: Unit Tests
nodes.rationale: Unit tests live in #[cfg(test)] beside the code, stay independent of shared mutable state, and check behavior rather than implementation.

nodes.label: Client Generators
nodes.rationale: Replace Rust and TypeScript stubs only after schema and migrations match SurrealDB. Generated types should follow links, optionals, nested objects, and edges so the client is not a shell of the DSL.

nodes.label: Codegen Stub Gap
nodes.rationale: generate --target rust and typescript emit struct or type shells with optionals and arrays, but not links, edges, or nested objects as real types, and no client. The source still marks them as stubs.

nodes.label: codegen crate
nodes.rationale: Language-agnostic codegen contracts so Rust and TypeScript generators plug in without the domain knowing a target language.

nodes.label: PhantomData
nodes.rationale: PhantomData carries the state type with no runtime field, so the state machine does not allocate extra memory.

nodes.label: Box at API Boundary
nodes.rationale: Boxing dyn Trait inside a struct drops static dispatch. Expose the trait object at the public boundary, not in internal fields.

nodes.label: Dynamic Dispatch
nodes.rationale: dyn Trait goes through a vtable. Use it for mixed collections, plugins, and a stable facade, and only when type erasure is required. It is slower and errors are less specific.

nodes.label: Generics
nodes.rationale: Generics are compile-time stand-ins so one definition serves many concrete types, including the markers used by the type state pattern.

nodes.label: Monomorphization
nodes.rationale: The compiler emits a copy of generic code per concrete type, so generics match concrete performance and cost compile time and binary size.

nodes.label: Object Safety
nodes.rationale: A trait object cannot have generic methods or a Self: Sized bound. Methods take self by reference or by value. Prefer &dyn Trait unless ownership or threads need Box or Arc.

nodes.label: Static Dispatch
nodes.rationale: impl Trait and trait bounds specialize and inline. Use them when the type is known at compile time and the path is hot.

nodes.label: Protocol State Machine
nodes.rationale: A disconnected client only has connect, and a connected client only has send, so sending before connecting does not compile.

nodes.label: Type State Pattern
nodes.rationale: States are types, not flags, so illegal transitions fail to compile. PhantomData markers are erased after compilation. Use the pattern when it prevents bugs; enums are enough for trivial states, and the signatures get verbose.

nodes.label: Typestate Builder
nodes.rationale: Required fields are type parameters, so build exists only after name and age are set. Optional fields such as email do not change the state.

nodes.label: Milestone 1 Offline Schema Toolchain
nodes.rationale: Ship parsing, validation, diffing, and SurrealQL rendering first. Live database commands were deferred so the domain and renderers could stabilize without a connectivity dependency. The source is scaffold commit 6fa7ad4 and the README; there was no separate inception plan.

nodes.label: Post-Plan Work on main
nodes.rationale: Field assignments, reverse-diff down migrations, naming blocks, id inference of record<table> with RecordId rejected, flexible objects, and real db push and migrate apply through the official client were not in the offline milestone. End-to-end tests use testcontainers and were not re-run without Docker.

nodes.label: COMPUTED Clause
nodes.rationale: @value and @updated stay VALUE, which is recomputed on write. COMPUTED is a separate read-time read-only clause and is intentionally not emitted. DEFAULT, VALUE, and COMPUTED now run in dependency order rather than field-name order.

nodes.label: DEFINE FIELD Compatibility
nodes.rationale: TYPE, option, array, record, FLEXIBLE, DEFAULT, DEFAULT ALWAYS, VALUE, READONLY, SCHEMAFULL, SCHEMALESS, UNIQUE, FULLTEXT, and raw PERMISSIONS still match 3.3.0, so no renderer change was required. FULLTEXT is the 3.x name; 2.x called the same feature SEARCH ANALYZER.

nodes.label: FLEXIBLE Semantics Change
nodes.rationale: FLEXIBLE now covers every object inside the type, including option<object>, array<object>, and object arms of a union. A type with no object is rejected. The validator already requires object for @flexible, so existing DSL checks already match the new engine rule.

nodes.label: id Field Enforcement
nodes.rationale: DEFINE FIELD id TYPE is enforced on write. @id renders as TYPE record<table>, so an id that is not a record of that table fails on insert. DEFAULT on id is allowed. DEFAULT ALWAYS on id is rejected because an explicit id must win. The DSL does not yet block @defaultAlways on @id.

nodes.label: SurrealDB Rust SDK Upgrade
nodes.rationale: The surrealdb crate moved from 2.6.5, while the manifest said 2.2, to 3.3.0. SDK 2.x cannot open a WebSocket to a 3.x server because of a subprotocol mismatch. Root sign-in now takes owned String credentials. The e2e image moved from the testcontainers-modules 0.15 hardcoded v2.2 tag to v3.3.0 via with_tag.

nodes.label: SurrealDB 3.3.0
nodes.rationale: Checked 2026-10-06. Latest stable server and Rust SDK are 3.3.0 from 24 Sep 2026. The repo tracks the 3.3 line. Patch 3.2.5 on 5 Oct 2026 stays on the previous line and is not the target. The README target moved from 3.1.5 to 3.3.0.

nodes.label: Awesome Schema
nodes.rationale: Schema modeling, migration, and code generation toolkit. Generic ORMs flatten databases and cannot faithfully model SurrealDB graph edges, record links, permissions, events, assertions, and vector indexes. A Prisma-like DSL stays close to native concepts while the core stays database-agnostic so new providers do not rewrite the CLI or migration engine.

nodes.label: Awesome Schema DSL
nodes.rationale: One awesome.schema file is the source of truth. It is meant to feel like a Prisma DSL while expressing datasource, model, edge, type, and provider extensions that generic tools drop.

nodes.label: Field Assignments
nodes.rationale: @default, @defaultAlways, @value, @updated, and @readonly map onto SurrealDB DEFINE FIELD clauses DEFAULT, DEFAULT ALWAYS, VALUE, and READONLY. @updated is an alias of VALUE for timestamps such as updatedAt. @readonly is meant to be used with @value so computed fields are not manually overwritten.

nodes.label: Flexible Object
nodes.rationale: object @flexible mirrors SurrealDB schemaless-in-schemafull nested data. Inline blocks, dotted paths, and reusable type definitions all render as TYPE object FLEXIBLE plus nested DEFINE FIELD statements, so authors are not forced into one nesting syntax.

nodes.label: SurrealDB
nodes.rationale: First target because 3.x combines document, graph, and schemafull or schemaless tables in one engine. Current target is 3.3.0. The first milestone started on 3.1.5 and chose to embrace that expressiveness rather than hide it behind a lowest-common-denominator model.

nodes.label: Roadmap Notes
nodes.rationale: Separates the original milestone, what the code check found, and the ordered backlog so new ideas are written into next.md instead of remaining only in chat.

nodes.label: samply
nodes.rationale: On macOS, samply is the better profiling interface than flamegraph.

nodes.label: smallvec
nodes.rationale: smallvec keeps small arrays inline and moves large ones to the heap.

nodes.label: Borrowing over Cloning
nodes.rationale: Clone when the original must be preserved, for Arc or Rc, or when an API demands owned data. Do not clone inside loops, clone large collections, or clone to hide a lifetime the caller should have transferred.

nodes.label: Copy Trait
nodes.rationale: Pass by value when every field is Copy and the value is about two or three words, up to 24 bytes, with no heap data. Enum size follows the largest variant. Large Copy arrays live on the stack and can overflow it.

nodes.label: Use Declaration Order
nodes.rationale: Group imports as std, external crates, workspace crates, then super and crate. rustfmt can enforce that. As of Rust 1.88, nightly rustfmt is required for correct reordering.

nodes.label: Iterators versus For Loops
nodes.rationale: For loops fit early exits and side effects. Iterator chains fit transforms because they are lazy and fuse into one loop. Prefer sum over fold, and iter over into_iter for Copy elements. Do not collect only to iterate again.

nodes.label: Option and Result Handling
nodes.rationale: Match when the inner value matters. let-else is for an expected early return, break, or continue. if-let is for an else branch that computes. Use ? when the Err value is irrelevant, and do not unwrap outside tests.

nodes.label: Prevent Early Allocation
nodes.rationale: or, map_or, unwrap_or, and ok_or evaluate their argument immediately, so the _else forms skip allocating strings or collections on the success path. inspect_err and map_err log and wrap Err.

nodes.label: Avoid Redundant Cloning
nodes.rationale: Clone only for a real owned copy: an API that demands it, a snapshot, Arc or Rc, a consuming builder, or a cheap handle such as a hyper client that shares a pool. Delay the clone until it is required. Prefer borrowed parameters otherwise.

nodes.label: Cow
nodes.rationale: std::borrow::Cow represents data that might be borrowed or owned, so the borrowed path does not allocate.

nodes.label: Measure Before Optimizing
nodes.rationale: Do not guess. Rust is already fast, dev profiles hide optimizations, and a microbenchmark gain under about 5 percent may not be worth keeping. Profiles and benches use --release.

nodes.label: Stack versus Heap
nodes.rationale: Keep small Copy values on the stack. Pass values over 512 bytes by reference. Box recursive types. Do not add inline unless a benchmark shows a win. Box::new of a huge array still builds it on the stack first.

nodes.label: Zero-Cost Iterators
nodes.rationale: Iterator adapters compile into tight loops. Pass the iterator onward instead of collecting an intermediate Vec.

nodes.label: FileSystemPort
nodes.rationale: Outbound port for read, write, and exists so use cases never touch a real filesystem and tests can substitute a fake.

nodes.label: ImportUsersCommand
nodes.rationale: Thin handler: map flags to input, read stdin when the path is a dash, execute, then pick JSON or human formatter. It does not contain import rules.

nodes.label: ImportUsersUseCase
nodes.rationale: Canonical use case: dry-run returns without saving, otherwise reads a file through a port, parses rows, and saves users. Empty input is NO_ROWS_FOUND.

nodes.label: OutputWriter
nodes.rationale: Stdout port used by formatters. Keeping write behind a trait lets JSON tests avoid a real terminal.

nodes.label: User
nodes.rationale: Entity built from value objects. getId throws ID_NOT_DEFINED until the repository assigns an id after insert, so identity is a persistence concern rather than a constructor input.

nodes.label: Cli
nodes.rationale: clap root named awesome-schema. Global options are flattened and subcommands nest Users then Import, matching one subcommand to one command handler.

nodes.label: ImportUsersInput
nodes.rationale: Domain-layer DTO only: file path, optional content, dry_run, and format. Handlers map flags into it and never pass raw argv into core.

nodes.label: User
nodes.rationale: Constructed from Email and StringValue. id() returns DomainError::IdNotDefined until set_id, which the repository calls after insert.

nodes.label: CLI Architecture Examples
nodes.rationale: Language-neutral pseudocode for the same import-users flow. Idiomatic Rust lives in RUST_EXAMPLES so this file stays a conceptual reference.

nodes.label: Breaking Change
nodes.rationale: Incompatible changes are marked with a bang after the type or scope, or with a BREAKING CHANGE footer.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits
nodes.rationale: Commits use type[optional scope]: description, plus an optional body and footer. Type and scope come from the diff so history stays semantic.

nodes.label: Analyze Diff
nodes.rationale: Read staged diff when the index is non-empty, otherwise the working tree, plus porcelain status, and choose type, scope, and message from that diff.

nodes.label: Commit Message Generation
nodes.rationale: The subject is present-tense imperative, under 72 characters, with one logical change per commit and issue references such as Closes #123.

nodes.label: Git Safety Protocol
nodes.rationale: Do not change git config, run destructive commands, skip hooks, or force-push main unless explicitly asked. A hook failure means a new commit, not an amend.

nodes.label: Intelligent File Staging
nodes.rationale: Stage one logical change at a time. Never commit secrets such as .env files, credentials, or private keys.

nodes.label: Real Graph Edges
nodes.rationale: edge and @relation parse today and then disappear or become ordinary tables. They should render as DEFINE TABLE TYPE RELATION and be diffed before LIGHTWEIGHT or INLINE relations are modeled, because those 3.3 features assume a normal relation already renders.

nodes.label: Index Kinds
nodes.rationale: Index.unique, fulltext, and vector already exist and the renderer can emit them, but the parser never sets the flags. @@index must grow those flags. On 3.3 a vector index is HNSW DIMENSION DIST, not the bare VECTOR keyword the renderer appends today.

nodes.label: Migration Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: migrate apply re-runs every migration.surql and never uses down files. A ledger, pending-only apply, reverse rollback, and status that distinguishes applied from pending are required before the migration loop is trustworthy. DropIndex and permission removal must also be emitted when the diff sees them.

nodes.label: SchemaDiffer
nodes.rationale: Must include edges, including edge fields, for create, alter, and drop. Today edge changes can parse without producing migration operations.

nodes.label: db push
nodes.rationale: Loads the schema, renders SurrealQL, and executes it with the official client. The README still calls this a stub, and this pass did not re-check it against a live database.

nodes.label: DropIndex Gap
nodes.rationale: DropIndex exists as a migration operation and the renderer emits REMOVE INDEX, but the differ never emits DropIndex when an index disappears, so removals cannot round-trip.

nodes.label: edge Block Gap
nodes.rationale: Edges parse and render as ordinary DEFINE TABLE plus fields. in and out are stored and never emitted, and migrate dev diffs models only, so edge changes produce no operations. They are not TYPE RELATION.

nodes.label: Index Flag Gap
nodes.rationale: Domain Index has unique, fulltext, and vector, and the renderer can emit them, but the parser always sets those flags false for @@index, so the DSL cannot yet express indexes the domain already models.

nodes.label: migrate apply Gap
nodes.rationale: The command executes each migration.surql, but there is no applied-migration ledger, so a second apply repeats the same files. Down files are never executed. It was not re-checked live in this pass.

nodes.label: README Drift
nodes.rationale: The README still says db push and migrate apply are stubs. The code and crates/e2e/tests/surrealdb_workflow.rs treat both as real commands. The db pull stub sentence remains accurate.

nodes.label: @relation Gap
nodes.rationale: Relation fields parse, for example posts to Post with a relation name, but the renderer skips any field with relation_name, so that field never appears in SurrealQL.

nodes.label: HNSW Vector Index
nodes.rationale: Vector indexes are HNSW DIMENSION DIST or DiskANN, not a bare VECTOR keyword. The renderer still appends VECTOR when Index.vector is set, but the parser never sets that flag, so current schemas do not emit the obsolete clause.

nodes.label: Relation Type Features
nodes.rationale: 3.2 to 3.3 adds TYPE RELATION IN OUT, LIGHTWEIGHT record-less relations with no fields, indexes, events, or SCHEMAFULL, INLINE on a relation field, and INLINE EDGES or INLINE REFERENCES on a vertex table. They belong with the graph-edge work and do not change SQL generated today.

nodes.label: edge block
nodes.rationale: Native edge blocks model SurrealDB graph relations with in and out endpoints, instead of collapsing them into Prisma or TypeORM join-style relations.

nodes.label: MigrationOperation
nodes.rationale: Domain-level change such as CreateTable, CreateField, or CreateIndex. Providers map these variants to DDL so the differ never emits SurrealQL directly.

nodes.label: MigrationRenderer
nodes.rationale: Port that renders a MigrationPlan as executable statements, so the differ stays provider-neutral and only the renderer speaks DDL.

nodes.label: Migration Workflow
nodes.rationale: migrate dev diffs the current schema against the latest snapshot.json, produces domain operations, and the SurrealDB renderer writes migration.surql and migration.down.surql. Down migrations are the reverse diff so rollback mirrors the forward change. The flow resembles TypeORM, but the intermediate form is domain operations rather than provider SQL.

nodes.label: Status Check 2026-10-06
nodes.rationale: Checked main at 4141758 by reading the CLI, domain, parser, differ, renderer, codegen, and db adapters. cargo test --workspace --exclude e2e passed 156 tests. crates/e2e was not run because it needs Docker. Done means unit or CLI coverage; partial means a named gap remains.

nodes.label: cargo clippy
nodes.rationale: Clippy catches performance, style, redundancy, and non-idiomatic code the compiler misses, so it belongs in the daily workflow and in CI. The Router repo exposes this as cargo xtask lint.

nodes.label: clone_on_copy
nodes.rationale: Catches clone on Copy types such as u32 and bool, where a copy is the operation that was meant.

nodes.label: large_enum_variant
nodes.rationale: A large variant inflates every value of the enum. Boxing the payload is the usual fix unless match speed matters more than size.

nodes.label: manual_ok_or
nodes.rationale: Suggests ok_or_else instead of a match that only converts Option into Result.

nodes.label: needless_collect
nodes.rationale: Stops an iterator from being collected when the allocation is thrown away by the next consumer.

nodes.label: redundant_clone
nodes.rationale: Flags clones that do not change ownership and that cost real time on large values.

nodes.label: expect over allow
nodes.rationale: allow hides a lint forever. expect fires again when the lint no longer applies, and the comment must say why. Keep overrides local; global allows are for cases like Bevy's default set.

nodes.label: Workspace Lint Configuration
nodes.rationale: Cargo.toml lint tables set level and priority so the higher-priority lint wins when two conflict, at package or workspace scope.

nodes.label: Arc
nodes.rationale: Arc is the atomic reference count for sharing across threads, often as Arc<Mutex<T>> or Arc<[T]>.

nodes.label: Box
nodes.rationale: Box is the single-owner heap pointer for large and recursive types. It is Send and Sync when T is.

nodes.label: Rc
nodes.rationale: Rc shares ownership on one thread and is neither Send nor Sync. A linked structure is the usual case.

nodes.label: Rust Atomics and Locks
nodes.rationale: Mara Bos's Rust Atomics and Locks is the cited reference for the pointer and locking model.

nodes.label: Interior Mutability
nodes.rationale: Cell mutates Copy data without &mut. RefCell checks borrows at runtime and can panic. Mutex and RwLock are the threaded forms; RwLock allows many readers or one writer.

nodes.label: Once and Lazy Initialization
nodes.rationale: OnceCell and LazyCell initialize once on one thread and are not Sync. OnceLock and LazyLock are the thread-safe forms, including static config.

nodes.label: Raw Pointers
nodes.rationale: const and mut pointers are for FFI and are unsafe. The programmer upholds aliasing and lifetimes. They are not Send or Sync by themselves.

nodes.label: Send and Sync
nodes.rationale: Send allows a value to move to another thread. Sync allows shared references across threads. A pointer is thread-safe only when the data behind it is.

nodes.label: Shared and Exclusive Borrows
nodes.rationale: &T allows many readers and is Send + Sync. &mut T allows one writer and is not Send. Both are the default over owning pointers.

nodes.label: anyhow
nodes.rationale: anyhow is for binaries that want ergonomic context. It erases the error type and scatters context strings, so libraries should not return anyhow::Result. Test helpers may.

nodes.label: thiserror
nodes.rationale: Library errors should be enums or structs derived with thiserror so Display, From, and ? stay consistent.

nodes.label: Async Error Bounds
nodes.rationale: Errors that cross await or task spawn must be Send + Sync + 'static. Libraries should avoid Box<dyn Error> unless erasure is required.

nodes.label: Avoid unwrap and expect
nodes.rationale: expect is clearer than unwrap, and both abort. Production code uses let-else, if-let, or the unwrap_or family. Tests and impossible failures may still unwrap.

nodes.label: Error Hierarchies
nodes.rationale: Layered systems nest errors with thiserror's from attribute so a service error wraps database and HTTP errors without hand-written From impls.

nodes.label: Question Mark Propagation
nodes.rationale: Prefer ? over match chains so errors bubble. Use map_err, or_else, or inspect_err only when recovering or logging.

nodes.label: Result over Panic
nodes.rationale: Fallible functions return Result. panic, todo, unreachable, and unimplemented are for tests, bugs, and states that have been proved impossible.

nodes.label: Architectural Decision Record
nodes.rationale: A decision that must outlive a pull request belongs in an ADR or a design doc, not in a long comment.

nodes.label: missing_docs
nodes.rationale: Libraries that want full coverage deny missing_docs. Related lints cover broken intra-doc links, empty docs, and missing Panics, Errors, and Safety sections.

nodes.label: non_exhaustive
nodes.rationale: Mark a public enum non_exhaustive when downstream crates match on it and new variants are expected.

nodes.label: Doc Comments
nodes.rationale: /// documents a public item: purpose, errors, panics, and examples that cargo test can run. //! documents the module or crate. Examples are also tests.

nodes.label: Line Comments
nodes.rationale: Double-slash comments are for safety, workarounds, platform quirks, and links to decisions. They are not compiled, so they rot. A prefix such as SAFETY makes the kind of note scannable.

nodes.label: TODO as Issues
nodes.rationale: A TODO without an owner is invisible. File a GitHub or Jira issue and cite it, for example TODO(issue #42).

nodes.label: resolveExitCode
nodes.rationale: Maps stable error codes through ERROR_CATALOG to a process status. INVALID_ARGUMENT is exit 2; catalogued business errors use their exit; everything else is 1.

nodes.label: Error Catalog
nodes.rationale: Stable SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE codes map to an exit code and a human message. JSON errors go to stderr. Stack traces appear only with --verbose so clients can branch on codes. Exit 3 is optional partial success.

nodes.label: anyhow
nodes.rationale: Reserved for unexpected infrastructure failures at the cli boundary in main and di. Business rules stay on DomainError so exit mapping remains a closed set of codes.

nodes.label: awesome-schema binary
nodes.rationale: The cli package example names the binary awesome-schema, placing this workspace's CLI on the hexagonal crate layout with core as a path dependency.

nodes.label: Cargo Workspace Layout
nodes.rationale: core is a library with no CLI dependencies. cli is the binary. Other crates may depend on core but never on cli, so compile-time isolation matches the hexagonal dependency rule. Split a single crate only when reuse or isolation is needed.

nodes.label: DomainError
nodes.rationale: Single thiserror enum. Variant names are PascalCase and code() returns SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for catalogs and JSON. clap parse failures exit 2 in main and are not DomainError variants.

nodes.label: resolve_exit_code
nodes.rationale: InvalidEmail exits 2. Other DomainError values use the error catalog exit or fall back to 1, keeping clap usage errors distinct from business failures.

nodes.label: thiserror
nodes.rationale: Used only in core to derive DomainError. Presentation does not invent a second business-error type.

nodes.label: db pull Not Implemented
nodes.rationale: SurrealDbIntrospector returns DomainError::NotImplemented. The CLI test db_pull.rs and the e2e test db_pull_is_not_implemented_yet expect that failure, so the stub is intentional and covered.

nodes.label: CLI Architecture Checklist
nodes.rationale: Verification list for the split core, composition root, naming, thin commands, exit codes, and use-case tests before a CLI is considered layered.

nodes.label: CLI Architecture Reference
nodes.rationale: Language-neutral layer, naming, flow, validation, and error rules. Rust is the primary target, but folder semantics and dependency direction stay fixed across languages.

nodes.label: Rust Implementation Guide
nodes.rationale: Rust form of the language-neutral layers: crates, traits, DomainError, manual AppContext, clap handlers, and test doubles. Folder semantics stay fixed even when Rust flattens them into modules.

nodes.label: Hexagonal CLI Anti-patterns
nodes.rationale: Fat main, println in use cases, logic in formatters, env reads, global OnceLock repositories, mixed stdout, god commands, subprocess-only tests, concrete adapters, logic in domain type files, inline construction, unwrap, and clap in core all collapse the hexagon or break piping and tests.

nodes.label: Rust Hexagonal Anti-patterns
nodes.rationale: unwrap, println, clap::Parser, concrete adapters, lazy_static pools, and Box<dyn Error> inside use cases, plus business logic in main's subcommand match, all leak presentation or infrastructure into core.

nodes.label: Incremental Strangle Migration
nodes.rationale: Extract one command at a time to a handler plus use case while legacy main still dispatches unknown commands. Delete legacy code only after every command has moved, so the CLI keeps working during the split.

nodes.label: Migration from Monolithic main.rs
nodes.rationale: Move verbs to subcommands, then input types, use cases, ports, adapters, AppContext, thin handlers, formatters, and exit codes, so behavior moves inward before the CLI is thinned.

nodes.label: Service to CLI Migration
nodes.rationale: Reuse crates/core, replace HTTP or GraphQL handlers with presentation commands, and swap the server entry for main.rs. The domain stays; only the driving adapter changes.

nodes.label: AppContext
nodes.rationale: Manual wiring in cli/src/di.rs. No service locator and no global OnceLock for repositories. Handlers receive wired commands and never construct use cases inline.

nodes.label: ImportUsersUseCase
nodes.rationale: Struct holds Arc<dyn Port> dependencies. execute takes ImportUsersInput only, and the parameter must be named port. Use cases never import clap, std::process, stdio, or adapter types.

nodes.label: mockall
nodes.rationale: Dev-dependency of core for port-trait mocks. Primary tests target use cases; subprocess tests stay sparse.

nodes.label: UserRepository
nodes.rationale: Object-safe trait in domain/repositories with Send + Sync so use cases can hold Arc<dyn UserRepository>. Generic methods are avoided unless async-trait is used consistently.

nodes.label: Sync versus Async Style
nodes.rationale: Pick one style per codebase. Sync suits file and blocking CLI tools. Async plus async-trait suits concurrent I/O. Mixing sync use cases with async ports breaks the execute signature and object safety.

nodes.label: AppLogger
nodes.rationale: Logging port whose level comes from --verbose. Logs go to stderr. Stdout stays command output only, and JSON mode must not mix logs into the pipe.

nodes.label: Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: core/services coordinates use cases such as wizards and file-type dispatch. It is not a port. Use cases must not call each other; an orchestrator does, so multi-step workflows stay explicit.

nodes.label: Shared Capability Package
nodes.rationale: Extract shared capability only when two or more deployables need the same integration. Its adapters depend on its domain only and are composed at the CLI di, not across packages.

nodes.label: Application Core Layer
nodes.rationale: Use case classes and optional orchestrators. They may depend only on the domain. Orchestrators return structured results or error codes and do not write to the terminal.

nodes.label: Configuration Precedence
nodes.rationale: CLI flags override environment, then the config file, then defaults. Resolved config is passed through di. Use cases never read env, so tests supply inputs without the process environment.

nodes.label: Domain Core Layer
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary and contracts of one bounded context: entities, repository ports, outbound service ports, input and output types, and domain events. It must not depend on CLI frameworks, argv, env, or infrastructure SDKs.

nodes.label: Forbidden Dependency Rules
nodes.rationale: Core must not reach infrastructure, terminal libraries, process exit, or CLI arg types. Handlers must not call repository adapters. Use cases must not call each other or touch argv and stdio. These rules keep the hexagon boundary intact.

nodes.label: Infrastructure Layer
nodes.rationale: Adapters, commands, formatters, exit codes, composition, and environment. Handlers must not call adapters except through di and bootstrap, so the use case remains the only application entry.

nodes.label: Thin Handler Rule
nodes.rationale: Handlers only parse, optionally prompt, call execute, and format, about 30 lines. Business rules stay in the use case so presentation cannot become a second domain model.

nodes.label: Validation Layers
nodes.rationale: The parser checks flags and exits 2. Use cases enforce business rules. Value objects enforce field invariants. Repository adapters treat database constraints as a last resort, so each layer rejects only what it can know.

nodes.label: db pull
nodes.rationale: The introspector is the remaining explicit stub. It should read INFO FOR DB and INFO FOR TABLE and map tables, fields, indexes, and relations back into DatabaseSchema. How a pulled schema is written is still an open choice.

nodes.label: Later Backlog
nodes.rationale: Events and functions already render as operations but have no DSL. Assertions and permissions are still a raw string. Additional providers reuse the existing renderer and introspector ports. The README line that still calls db push and migrate apply stubs should be corrected.

nodes.label: cli crate
nodes.rationale: Binary awesome-schema. Orchestration only: di.rs wires adapters and clap exposes commands. No business logic lives in the CLI.

nodes.label: Connectivity Stubs
nodes.rationale: The README says db pull, db push, and migrate apply are intentionally stubbed so this milestone stays on parsing, validation, diffing, and SurrealQL rendering rather than live connectivity.

nodes.label: core crate
nodes.rationale: Owns the database-agnostic domain: models, fields, indexes, edges, migration operations, port traits, and use cases. SurrealDB-specific logic stays out of core so another provider does not fork the domain.

nodes.label: MigrationStore
nodes.rationale: Port that loads and saves schema snapshots so diffs do not read the migrations directory from inside the domain.

nodes.label: Planned Database Providers
nodes.rationale: Planned providers are surrealdb, mongodb, postgres, mysql, and sqlite. Each implements SchemaRenderer and MigrationRenderer, maps MigrationOperation to DDL, optionally implements SchemaIntrospector, and is registered in di.rs from datasource.provider.

nodes.label: renderers crate
nodes.rationale: Provider-specific DDL. SurrealDB is first. A new provider implements the renderer ports here or in crates/providers without changing core.

nodes.label: SchemaIntrospector
nodes.rationale: Port for pulling a live schema. db pull depends on it, and it is optional when adding a provider.

nodes.label: SchemaRenderer
nodes.rationale: Port that renders a full schema as provider DDL. Keeping it in core lets generate and db push share one render path per provider.

nodes.label: SchemaSource
nodes.rationale: Port that loads the DSL file. Use cases depend on the port so tests can supply schema text without the filesystem.

nodes.label: SurrealDB-First Policy
nodes.rationale: Stay on SurrealDB until the schema the DSL already accepts is what migrations and the database actually apply. Other providers wait so a second backend is not added before the first renderer matches the engine.

nodes.label: Hexagonal Architecture
nodes.rationale: core owns the database-agnostic domain, ports, and use cases. parser, migrations, renderers, and codegen implement or support those ports. cli only composes them in di.rs. SurrealDB-specific logic stays out of core, migrations, and cli commands so another provider is an adapter registration.
